key_idea: Enumerate the 2^c column subsets; a row set works iff every row is monotone on the subset and all consecutive chosen rows share the same per-column comparison pattern, which is a tiny chain DP over rows.
sketch: For each column mask S get the bitmask of rows increasing/decreasing on S incrementally from S minus its lowest bit (AND with a precomputed 'row has a[j]<a[k]' mask). Among valid rows count chains: f[x][b] = 1 + sum of f[y][x] over y with (P[y][x]&S)==(P[x][b]&S), where P is the column-wise less-than mask of two rows; columns are monotone exactly when all consecutive patterns are equal. Add the number of valid rows for single-row grids. Worst case about 2^20 * 20^3/6 simple operations, ~1.3 s locally. Answer up to 2^40 so use 64-bit. Stress-tested against brute force.
